title: Subsets
prompt:
Given an array of **unique** integers, return all possible subsets (the power set), in any order, no duplicates.

**Example**: `[1,2,3]` → `[[],[1],[2],[1,2],[3],[1,3],[2,3],[1,2,3]]`.

The backtracking template exactly as written in the pattern lesson.
hints: Record a COPY of path at every recursion node — every state along the way is a subset.
The `start` parameter prevents picking earlier elements again — that's what makes them subsets, not permutations.

solution.explanation: 2ⁿ subsets, O(n · 2ⁿ) total. Every node of the recursion tree IS a subset (record unconditionally); `start` enforces increasing indices so each combination appears exactly once.
